subject: PHI dataflow mapping & BAA boundary — clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Dr. Laura Mendoza <laura.mendoza@medsystems.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@medsystems.com
Date: 2026-11-10T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Inquiry: Can Redwood support PHI / BAA for our integration?

Hi Irene,

Quick intro — I'm Laura, Head of Integrations at MedSystems. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will route clinical notes (limited set of structured fields + free text clinician notes) into an LLM-powered summarization pipeline. Before we go too far in the POC, legal and security have asked two quick questions:

1) Does Redwood sign a BAA to cover PHI? If so, for which deployment modes (hosted API vs. dedicated vs. private)?
2) What controls/data boundary guarantees do you provide around PHI handling (ingress/egress, logs, backups, key management)?

I've attached a brief summary of the data elements we expect to send and a rough dataflow sketch. If Redwood can't cover PHI on your hosted tiers, could you indicate the path to move to a compliant setup?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call this week.

—Laura
Dr. Laura Mendoza
Head of Integrations, MedSystems
laura.mendoza@medsystems.com

Attachments: medsystems_phi_scope_attachment_summary.pdf; medsystems_dataflow_sketch.png

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Laura Mendoza <laura.mendoza@medsystems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support PHI / BAA for our integration?

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments (received). Short answer up front: yes, Redwood can support PHI, but it depends on the deployment mode and the contractual boundary. A BAA is available for Dedicated and Private deployments; our hosted public API is not eligible for PHI/BAA.

To give you a concise path forward:
- Hosted API: not HIPAA-eligible; do not send PHI.
- Dedicated: eligible for a BAA when contracted (reserved capacity pools isolated per customer, audit controls, config options).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): eligible and recommended for the highest compliance needs (customer-managed network, optional on-prem package).

Security controls we typically confirm as part of a BAA/DPIA: encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), encryption at rest (AES-256), customer-managed KMS options, audit logging with configurable retention, strict access controls, and documented operational procedures for backups and deletion. We'll need a dataflow mapping (what fields are PHI, where they land, any downstream persistence) and a short DPIA/processing description from your side to scope the BAA appropriately.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please share a redacted dataflow mapping (you already included a sketch — if you can label PHI elements explicitly that helps).
2) We'll send a short Redwood BAA request form and DPIA template for you to fill out (I attached the request form).
3) Schedule a 30-minute technical sync (Karthik — can you take the technical call?)

Happy to schedule a call tomorrow or Thursday — what works for you?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Trust & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_baa_request_form.docx

From: Dr. Laura Mendoza <laura.mendoza@medsystems.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@medsystems.com
Date: 2026-11-12T08:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support PHI / BAA for our integration?

Irene / team — thanks for the quick reply. I've annotated the sketch and marked which fields we consider PHI (patient identifiers, certain free-text sections). See attached updated sketch and scope doc. A few clarifying Qs from our security team inline:

- Are ephemeral request logs retained outside customer-controlled storage for Dedicated? If so, what is the default retention and can it be shortened?
- For Private/VPC, do you offer an option where the KV cache and model artifacts remain on customer-controlled volumes?
- Does Redwood support HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest on Dedicated (we prefer KMS/HSM with customer control)?

We can take a 30-minute technical call on 2026-11-13 at 10:00 AM ET. Is Karthik available?

—Laura

Attachments: medsystems_phi_scope_attachment_summary_v2.pdf; medsystems_dataflow_sketch_annotated.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Laura Mendoza <laura.mendoza@medsystems.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: Can Redwood support PHI / BAA for our integration?

Laura — thanks for the annotated materials and for scheduling the call. Quick answers up front based on how our product shapes up today: 

1) Request logs (Dedicated): by default, short-lived operational logs are kept for 30 days; we can reduce retention to customer-specified windows as part of the Dedicated contract and logging config. Persistent audit logs for compliance can be forwarded to your SIEM (S3/BigQuery) and retained per your retention policy.

2) KV cache & artifacts (Private/VPC): for Private deployments we support customer-managed volumes — model artifacts and KV cache can be mounted on customer-controlled storage if required (on-prem package or VPC with mounted volumes). For Dedicated, model artifacts are in an isolated tenant store managed by Redwood; we can provide export policies and additional isolation guarantees in the BAA.

3) KMS/HSM: we offer integrations with customer KMS providers (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS) and can support HSM-backed keys in Private deployments; for Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys where cloud provider features allow. We'll surface exact key management options in the BAA annex.

Next steps:
- I'll run a short internal tech checklist against your annotated sketch and surface any ingestion edge cases before our 11/13 call.
- Irene will share the Redwood BAA request form and a DPIA template by end of day.

If anything changes on timing, ping me — otherwise see you on the call.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
